title: [CQ-R09] Validated source snapshot transfer
description:
Objective: Export protected base manifests and actual overlay bytes and reject unsafe imports.

Deliverable: Validated source snapshot transfer. This is task R09 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): R08.
definitionOfDone: Path traversal, symlink escapes and .git/.moe/control-path writes are refused.
Hash identities are derived from transferred bytes, not writer declarations.
No host repo/home/SSH/provider-control filesystem is mounted in guest.
Fresh verification `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.

implementationPlan.description:
Supervisor export mode plus its supervisor test rows (X1-X3).

Read first: the landed CQ-R09c contract this step builds on. That is guest-supervisor.py's materialize(), WORKSPACE, WORKSPACE_MANIFEST and the manifest's JSON shape {"version": 1, "digest": hex, "files": {path: [executable, size, sha256]}}, plus R09c's materialize test rows in scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs. Do not change that contract. If R09c landed it differently, follow the landed code and record the deviation in your step note.

Implement the export mode in scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py.

main():
- Accept exactly ['export'] beside ['bridge'] and ['materialize']; every other argv stays EX_USAGE (64).
- A non-root euid gives EX_NOPERM (77) before anything is read.
- ['export'] at euid 0 returns export(1).

export(out_fd, workspace=WORKSPACE, manifest=WORKSPACE_MANIFEST, drop=drop_to_agent):
1. Still root, read the manifest:
   - os.open with O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK; fstat must show a regular file of at most MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES = 16 MiB;
   - json.loads must give the exact shape above: each sha256 64 lowercase hex, each size a non-negative int, each executable a bool.
   Then open the workspace root with O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW. Any failure here exits EX_DATAERR (65) with no frame.
2. drop(): os.setgroups([]), then os.setgid and os.setuid to the AGENT_IDENTITY account's gid and uid (from pwd.getpwnam), in that order, before the first workspace entry is opened. From then on the walk reads only what the agent itself could read, so a root-only file stays unreadable however it is reached. A drop failure (KeyError for a missing account, or OSError) exits EX_OSERR (71) with no frame.
3. Walk from the root fd using directory fds only:
   - per directory, list names with os.scandir on the fd and sort them by os.fsencode bytes. A name that is not valid UTF-8 must still sort; it reaches the host as a lone-surrogate escape through encode_frame's backslashreplace, and the host refuses it. Never .encode('utf-8') a listed name strictly;
   - lstat each name with dir_fd and follow_symlinks=False;
   - descend only into a real directory, through os.open(name, O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, dir_fd=parent), and close each fd on every path. Never enter or read through a symlink.
4. Regular files:
   - open with O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and dir_fd. fstat must still show a regular file with the lstat's (st_dev, st_ino), else exit EX_IOERR (74);
   - read in OUTPUT_CHUNK_BYTES chunks, hashing with sha256; executable is st_mode & 0o100;
   - if the manifest holds the same [executable, size, sha256] for that path, emit nothing;
   - otherwise emit {kind:'file', path, executable, size}, then one {kind:'data', data: base64} frame per chunk. An empty file gets no data frame.
5. A symlink gives {kind:'symlink', path}. Any other non-directory (FIFO, socket, device) gives {kind:'special', path}. Neither is opened or read.
6. After the walk:
   - emit {kind:'delete', path} for each manifest path that was not seen at all, in UTF-8 byte order;
   - then emit {kind:'end', entries: N}, where N counts the file, symlink, special and delete frames;
   - exit 0.
7. Bounds. Each of these exits EX_DATAERR (65) with no end frame:
   - more than 10,000 emitted entries (R09a MAX_IMPORT_ENTRIES);
   - more than 268,435,456 bytes of changed file data, checked from fstat before reading;
   - a relative path over 1024 UTF-8 bytes, checked before descending, which also bounds recursion depth and open fds;
   - more than WALK_LIMIT = 100,000 names visited.
   A write failure or read error exits EX_IOERR (74). Outside the frames above, no traceback, path or file byte ever reaches stdout.

Update the header comment's mode list and exit codes, and say why the walk runs as the agent.

Error handling is part of this step: every OSError path maps to one fixed exit code, and fds close on every path. Reuse R09c's Python helpers where they fit (frame reading, digest framing) instead of duplicating them.

Tests: rows X1-X3 in a new 'CQ-R09' section of scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs.
- Load the real file with the bridge test's importlib seam: copy LOAD and harness from scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs, or reuse R09c's copy if it added one.
- Run python3 -I -B. -B is mandatory, because both IDE bundlers ship scripts/local-runner wholesale and would ship a __pycache__. Never add a CLI test mode.
- Skip these rows on win32 with a reason (POSIX python3 only).
- Build each workspace and manifest with R09c's materialize() through the same seam, injecting workspace, manifest and owner = the current uid and gid. Pass drop=lambda: None unless the row tests the drop.
- Decode stdout with createFrameDecoder.

Rows:
- X1 CLI surface: ['export', 'x'] and ['EXPORT'] exit 64 with empty stdout; main(['export'], geteuid=lambda: 1000) gives 77 with empty stdout. The existing bridge and materialize rows still pass.
- X2 An unchanged workspace emits only {kind:'end', entries: 0}. Each of these produces exactly the expected frames: one edit, one chmod +x, one new nested file, one delete, a symlink to a file, a symlink to a directory (never descended: a file beneath its target is not reported) and a FIFO. A file's data decodes to its bytes, and no frame carries a sha256, oid or digest.
- X3 Failures:
  - a missing, symlinked or malformed manifest, a missing workspace, and a workspace that is a symlink each give 65 with empty stdout;
  - with os.setgroups, os.setgid and os.setuid patched to record calls, the drop happens in that order before the first workspace os.open (record os.open calls too). A drop that raises gives 71 with empty stdout;
  - 10,001 new empty files give 65 with no end frame.

Verification. Run it once, fresh, from the repo root:
`node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-snapshot.test.mjs`
This is the CI local-runner step, and it includes DoD 4's `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs`.

On WSL, run it with `env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin node --test ...` so the Windows PATH stays out. Exit 0 is required, and its output tail is the complete_task verification evidence.

Also confirm:
- no scripts/local-runner/__pycache__ exists;
- `git diff --numstat` over this task's three files is within the size rail;
- `pgrep -af 'time[.]sleep[(]600'` shows nothing of yours.
Do not touch peers' dirty paths: note them in your step note and continue.

Error handling for the gate itself: if a test fails, fix the cause with a test, never by weakening or skipping a row, then re-run the whole command.

comments.author: architect-26ba32c3
comments.content: Note for R09's planner (2026-10-25): C02 (task-b23c65b0, the daemon's bounded repository source provider) no longer depends on R09; the operator re-sliced it to run now. C02 treats a full Git COMMIT id as the immutable manifest. It reads committed blobs only, through the hardened openProjectGit envelope, and reports uncommitted/overlay bytes explicitly as unsupported (limitation 'committed-bytes-only'). If R09's exported base manifest or overlay is later meant to feed the daemon provider, either expose it as a commit/tree identity C02 can read, or plan an explicit adapter task. Do not change C02's refusal semantics silently.

comments.author: architect-4c57a52b
comments.content:
Split on 2026-10-26 (architect-4c57a52b; the operator chose this in the REPL). The original row is too big for one 400-LOC task, and its transfer half needs the CQ-R08 bridge, which is still three slices away. Following the epic's M01/C02/R08 pattern, this row keeps its full DoD as the FINAL slice. It depends on:
- CQ-R08 (task-7a77465621dc4d6588d5747394cb0ced), which closes the guest-supervisor chain.
- CQ-R09a (task-491a2d8cff4d45afbdac79539098ebb1, PLANNING). This is the pure host-side import gate, scripts/local-runner/source-snapshot.mjs:
  - it refuses traversal and non-portable paths, control paths, every symlink, and case and ancestor collisions;
  - it derives size and sha256 from a private copy of the transferred bytes and refuses writer-declared identities;
  - its tests are in the new scripts/tests/local-runner-snapshot.test.mjs, registered in CI.
  It touches no R08 file, so it runs in parallel now.

Control paths (operator decision): any segment equal, case-insensitively, to .git, .gitmodules, .moe, .mcp.json, .claude, .codex, .gemini, .grok or .worktrees, at any depth. NTFS and HFS lookalikes are refused through the portability rules.

What remains for this row, to plan after both land. It will likely need a further SPIDR split then.
1. Host export of the PROTECTED base manifest: read-only Git plumbing on a full commit id (ls-tree -r -z, cat-file --batch). Identities are the host's own, computed through source-snapshot.mjs. Also the ACTUAL overlay bytes of the dirty paths. Per the C02 note above: if the base must feed the daemon's repository provider, expose a commit/tree identity C02 can read, or plan an adapter task.
2. Transfer by copy only, over multipass exec stdin or `multipass transfer`, never a mount. Re-check R07's zero-mount boundary evidence around the transfer (DoD 3).
3. Guest side, in guest-supervisor.py after R08: materialize the snapshot into the workspace, and export the candidate overlay back. CQ-R10 owns attempt workspaces and identities, so keep that boundary explicit.
4. Host import: parse the transport into R09a entries and pass every one through validateImport (DoD 1 and 2).

Suggested verification for this row: `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-snapshot.test.mjs`, a superset of the DoD command.

R09a deliberately refuses ALL symlinks. Permitting contained ones would need base-manifest awareness (writes beneath a base symlink), which CQ-R12 admission must handle in any case.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) One R09 task under a ~1,250-line size exception. The operator rejected it in the architect REPL on 2026-10-27 in favour of a 3-way split: R09b export (task-697fb2de), R09c materialize (task-4af8b8c1), and this row for export back plus host import.
2) A host-side diff, with the guest streaming its whole workspace. Rejected: it moves every repository byte on every import and hits R09a's 10,000-entry / 256 MiB caps on medium repos, while the supervisor already holds a root-only manifest of exactly what it materialized.
3) Guest tar, or `multipass transfer`. Rejected: Node has no tar parser, so the host would have to parse an untrusted archive format, and transfer writes as the default user into a path the host must then trust.
4) Walking the export as root. Rejected: between lstat and open, an agent could swap a name for a link to a root-only file such as the supervisor credential. Dropping to the agent identity first bounds every read to what the agent could already read, and O_NOFOLLOW plus the dev/ino check still refuse links.
5) Filtering control paths or symlinks in the guest. Rejected: the host gate must see them and refuse them (DoD 1), so the supervisor reports them and validateImport refuses the whole candidate.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
ASSUMED interfaces, not landed when this plan was written. The X-rows pin each one so that drift fails loudly. If R09b or R09c QA changes one, amend this plan with moe.amend_plan_step rather than re-blocking.
- CQ-R09c (task-4af8b8c17d1f4949b0d85e24e69f986f):
  - scripts/local-runner/snapshot-transfer.mjs exports SNAPSHOT_CHUNK_BYTES; workspaceEntries(snapshot); snapshotArgv(name, mode) for 'materialize' or 'export'; assertNoMounts(name, provider), throwing TRANSFER_MOUNTS_PRESENT or TRANSFER_MOUNTS_UNKNOWN; runSupervisorStream({name, mode, provider, timeoutMs, input, onFrame}), where an onFrame throw kills the provider and rejects with that same error; and materializeSnapshot({name, snapshot, provider, timeoutMs}).
  - guest-supervisor.py: WORKSPACE='/var/lib/moe/workspace'; WORKSPACE_MANIFEST='/var/lib/moe/workspace.manifest.json', holding {"version":1,"digest":hex,"files":{path:[executable,size,sha256]}}; materialize(in_fd, out_fd, workspace, manifest, owner); exit codes 65 (EX_DATAERR), 73 (EX_CANTCREAT) and 74.
- CQ-R09b (task-697fb2de19324ccb851defaf9f24043b): scripts/local-runner/source-export.mjs exports exportSourceSnapshot({repoDir, commit, git, timeoutMs}), resolving {version:1, commit, tree, base, overlay, excluded}.

LANDED facts:
- guest-supervisor.py (R08b/c, R10a): write_frame is the only stdout writer. Exit codes 0/64/71/74/75/76/77/78 are taken. main() gates the euid through an injectable geteuid. Tests load the file with python3 -I -B and importlib (LOAD and harness in local-runner-bridge.test.mjs), never through a CLI test mode.
- source-snapshot.mjs (R09a): validateImport is the only admission gate. It refuses kind 'symlink' with SNAPSHOT_SYMLINK_DENIED and any unknown kind with SNAPSHOT_ENTRY_INVALID. snapshotError, MAX_IMPORT_ENTRIES and MAX_IMPORT_BYTES are exported.
- guest-bridge.mjs: createFrameDecoder(max) returns decoded plain objects and poisons itself on error. MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES is 262,144, and an OUTPUT_CHUNK_BYTES chunk (65,536 raw, 87,384 as base64) fits it. isCanonicalBase64 is a Buffer round trip.
- guest-readiness.mjs: readGuestInfo and runGuestProbe(name, 'mountinfo') are the mount evidence.
- local-runner.test.mjs imports every module statically at the top, so one missing module fails the whole file. Its fakeGuest, healthy(), guestDetail() and mountinfo() fixtures fake info and the probes.
planningNotes.risks:
- Size: the operator approved this slice at about 430 lines in the split preview, and an R09c/R09 size-exception rail is proposed. Measure with git diff --numstat early; comments and blank lines count.
- Masking traps: build each hostile stream so exactly one rule fails, so that no missing check can hide behind another.
- Non-UTF-8 names: Python lists them as surrogate escapes. Sort with os.fsencode, and let encode_frame's backslashreplace carry the escape so the host's wellFormed check refuses it.
- A directory replaced by a file, or the reverse, yields delete 'a/b' plus file 'a', which R09a refuses as an ancestor collision. The whole candidate is refused; this is a known v1 limit that R12 may refine.
- A file the agent itself made chmod 000 is unreadable after the drop. Export exits 74 and the import is refused (fail closed).
- The privilege drop is irreversible, so read the manifest and open the root fd before it. Tests patch os.setgroups, os.setgid and os.setuid, because a non-root runner cannot drop.
- Windows: only rows that need POSIX python3 skip on win32. Host rows with fake providers run everywhere, since CI runs ubuntu, macos and windows. On WSL, use the env -i Linux node 24 PATH (Serena gotcha-local-runner-tests).
- Hangs and orphans: give async rows a timeout and kill python children in t.after. After any mutation sweep, check pgrep -af 'time[.]sleep[(]600' for leftovers of your own.
- Out of scope: running the job, per-attempt workspaces and admission into host Git (R10/R12). verified-local and executionReady stay unchanged.
